subject: Per-tenant storage policy parameterization request
messages:
From: Julien Moreau <julien@greenline.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Per-tenant storage policy parameterization request

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this early look — Greenline’s compliance team has flagged the need for more granular controls around where customer data is stored and for how long. High level asks: per-tenant selection of storage region (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1), retention windows configurable per-tenant down to 30 days granularity, and a documented deletion workflow that produces an audit log for each deletion event.

We also need to understand how keying will work — whether tenant-specific keys are available or we must rely on Redwood-managed KMS. Attached is a short regulatory matrix that outlines country-level constraints (France/Germany: data at rest in-country preferred).

Can we schedule a 30-minute discovery next week to align on feasibility and a rough timeline? We’re targeting an internal compliance review by the end of Q1.

Best,
Julien
Compliance, Greenline Finance

Attachments: greenline_regulatory_matrix_v1.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Julien Moreau <julien@greenline.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Per-tenant storage policy parameterization request

Julien — thanks for the clear summary and the matrix. Looping in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (product) to scope this technically and map to our roadmap.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Quick discovery call (30m) to confirm exact retention granularity and encryption/keying expectations.
- Share a minimal requirements checklist so we can validate existing capabilities vs gaps.
- Optional: provide a sample tenant-data schema so we can evaluate whether per-tenant object routing is sufficient or if we need changes to the storage abstraction.

I’ve attached a quick checklist we use for these asks — please fill and return before the call if possible. Proposed times: Tue 2026-12-08 10:00 or Wed 2026-12-09 14:00 CET.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.example

Attachments: per-tenant-requirements-checklist.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Julien Moreau <julien@greenline.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Per-tenant storage policy parameterization request

Thanks for looping me in. A few questions from the infra side so we can scope effort: 
1) Tenant routing: do you expect an active selection per-tenant (admin UI/API) or a policy-based mapping from tenant attributes (country -> region)?
2) KMS: do you need tenant-owned keys (bring-your-own-key) or is customer-managed keys via our KMS integration acceptable?
3) Retention granularity: you asked for 30-day granularity — do you need per-object TTL, per-tenant default + overrides per-data-class, or both?
4) Cross-region failover: if a tenant pins to eu-west-1 but we must failover, do we need to copy all data or allow a temporary proxy with encrypted transit only?

Initial thoughts: we already have region-tagged storage buckets and soft-delete lifecycle hooks, but we don’t currently surface per-tenant TTLs in the control plane. Implementing tenant-level TTL + per-tenant region pinning will touch: routing layer (to ensure reads/writes land in the right region), control plane for configs, and deletion audit logs for SOC evidence. Ballpark engineering work: 6–8 engineer-weeks plus QA and a canary rollout. I’ll open INF-4572 and link some tech notes.

Link: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/INF-4572

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Julien Moreau <julien@greenline.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Cc: Greenline Legal <legal@greenline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-10T08:49:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Per-tenant storage policy parameterization request

Grace — quick clarifications from our side (apologies for the brief reply):
- Policy mapping: we prefer an explicit per-tenant selection in the admin console/API (to avoid mistakes from automated heuristics).
- KMS: Greenline requires tenant-managed keys for production tenants in scope (we can use Redwood’s KMS integration for test/dev).
- Retention: per-tenant default with per-data-class overrides; 30-day resolution is acceptable.
- Failover: soft-failover is acceptable for the first phase; we’ll want a read-only replicated mode in phase 2.

We’re aiming to sign off on a vendor readiness plan by 2027-03-31 — if you can give a rough roadmap and acceptance criteria we’ll include it in the compliance pack.

Thanks,
Julien

Subject: Re: Per-tenant storage policy parameterization request — roadmap ask

Team — putting this up as a formal roadmap request and acceptance criteria for Q1 planning. Greenline is a strategic financial customer and needs the following minimal deliverables in phase 1: 

Feature set requested (phase 1):
- Admin/API: explicit per-tenant region selection (eu-west-1 | eu-central-1) exposed in Console and via REST.
- Keying: KMS integration for BYOK (tenant-provided keys) with documented onboarding flow (test/dev via Redwood-managed KMS; prod via BYOK).
- Retention: per-tenant default TTL with per-data-class override; UI to set TTL in 30-day increments with server-side enforcement.
- Deletion & audit: deterministic deletion job + immutable audit trail entries for deletion events (satisfies SOC evidence).
- Canary: support for tenant-scoped canary (enable feature for a single tenant before rollout).

Acceptance criteria (min):
- All writes for a tenant pinned to selected region with end-to-end encryption using the tenant’s key (or Redwood-managed key for test).
- Deletion events produce immutable audit log records with timestamp + operator id + objects affected.
- Admin/API surface documented with examples and an E2E test that runs in our CI.

Scope request: Karthik, please provide a 2-week implementation estimate (engineering-weeks) for phase 1 by 2026-12-22. Marissa, please slot this ask into the Q1 roadmap draft and identify any product dependencies. Lauren — I’ll need your help with customer comms and the compliance pack once we have an estimate.

Linking the JIRA here: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/INF-4572
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/deal/GF-2026-1019

Thanks — Grace
